Rules / Cleanup

SK0240 The control flow does nothing

A jump, a default: section, a catch, an empty finally, an else on a branch that never falls through, or a switch-expression arm whose value the arm below it repeats — control flow that transfers to where control was already going.

CategoryCleanup
Default severitywarning
ScopeSyntax
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseyes
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floor—
Since2.0
SupersedesRedundantEmptySwitchSection, RedundantCatchClause, RedundantEmptyFinallyBlock, RedundantCaseLabel, RedundantEnumCaseLabelForDefaultSection, RedundantIfElseBlock, RedundantSwitchExpressionArms

Why

⚠ `catch (X) { throw; }` is the member that matters and the other two are housekeeping beside it. A rethrowing catch reads as error handling: it is where a reader goes looking for the recovery, the wrapping, the logging — and there is none. throw; preserves the stack trace, so unlike SK2015's throw ex; there is not even a defect underneath it; the clause is inert, and every question it raises has the answer "nothing happens here", which is what the code would say with no catch at all. The other two shapes are the same sentence about ordinary control flow: a continue; at the end of a loop body jumps to the next iteration that was one statement away, a return; at the end of a void body leaves a method that was about to end, and a default: section that only breaks describes what a switch with no matching section already does.

Example

Instead of:

try {
    Write(path, payload);
} catch (IOException) {
    throw;
}

Write:

Write(path, payload);

The ReSharper mapping

⚠ Seven ReSharper inspections, one concept, and the last two were measured against jb inspectcode 2025.2.6 rather than read off the export. RedundantIfElseBlock is a hint there and RedundantSwitchExpressionArms a warning; Skala reports the concept at warning. ⚠ RedundantSwitchExpressionArms does not mean what its name suggests: b switch { true => 1, false => 2, _ => 3 } is CS8510, a compiler error, and a non-exhaustive switch whose arms all agree is CS8509 — what ReSharper reports is an arm whose value the arm below it repeats. ⚠ Nothing in the SDK hosts either: absent from all 442 descriptors read out of SDK 10.0.400's analyzer assemblies, and silent in a probe with all 120 IDE and all 320 CA ids at warning where IDE0055, IDE0160, IDE0290, IDE0380 and CA1051 fired and no AD0001 was raised. IDE0046 is a different concept — it wants the if/else rewritten as a conditional expression, and it declined the throwing shape entirely.

When it does not fire

⚠ Only the last `catch` of a `try` is ever reported, and that is correctness rather than caution. Deleting an earlier one changes which handler an exception reaches: in try { … } catch (IOException) { throw; } catch (Exception e) { Log(e); } the first clause is what stops an IOException being logged, so removing it is a behaviour change wearing a redundancy's clothes. Removing the last clause can only leave the exception propagating, which is what the rethrow already did. A catch carrying a when filter is never reported: the filter runs code, and a filter that returns false leaves the exception to a later clause. ⚠ Where the rethrowing `catch` is the only one and there is no `finally`, the fix has to replace the whole `try` by its block's contents — try { … } alone is CS1524 — and that is offered only when the block declares nothing, because unwrapping a scope moves every local, local function and label it holds into the enclosing scope where a name that was never in conflict can now collide. A try block that declares a local is left alone rather than fixed badly, and so the finding is withheld. The same is true when the try is an embedded statement rather than a statement in a block, because the splice would have more than one statement and nowhere to put it. ⚠ `goto default;` anywhere in the switch withdraws the `default:` finding, because the section is the jump's target and deleting it turns a redundancy into CS0159. A default: sharing its section with a case label is a different shape and is not matched. ⚠ The `return;` half reads the written return type and never a symbol, so it matches the void keyword, constructors, destructors and set/init/add/remove accessors. async Task is the same redundancy and is deliberately not matched: Task is a name that can be aliased, and answering it needs a semantic model this rule does not ask for. ⚠ There is no iterator guard, and the belief that one was needed is refuted. A bare return; inside an iterator is not legal C# and does not mean yield break: the compiler rejects it with CS1622. The guard was written, committed with a negative fixture, and the fixture failed to compile — an iterator cannot contain the shape this rule matches, so nothing has to exclude it. ⚠ A comment or a preprocessor directive inside the span withdraws the finding. The fix deletes the span, default: break; // nothing to do for the rest is the author answering the question the reader was about to ask, and a cleanup that silently deletes prose has made the file worse than it found it. ⚠ The boolean-expression members of this family — RedundantBoolCompare, DoubleNegationOperator, NegativeEqualityExpression, RedundantTernaryExpression, RedundantLogicalConditionalExpressionOperand — are not covered. Each needs to know an operand's type before it is redundant rather than meaningful (x == true is not redundant for a bool?, and ! may be overloaded), which would make this rule semantic and stop it running on a loose file. RedundantIfElseBlock, RedundantCaseLabel and RedundantEnumCaseLabelForDefaultSection are not covered either. ⚠ The `else` shape is decided by the *then* branch and the test is syntactic: a block whose last statement is a jump cannot fall out of its end, so a true here is always right and everything else is declined — an if/else where both arms return, a while (true), an exhaustive switch are all missed rather than wrong. A directive anywhere inside the then branch withdraws the finding, because #if TRACE return; #endif ends in a jump in one configuration and falls through in the other and the parse the analyzer sees is one of the two. The else block is unwrapped only when it declares no local, local function or label — the same escaping-scope rule as the sole-catch unwrap — and only when the if itself sits directly in a block, because a parent that is not a block has exactly one embedded statement position. ⚠ The switch-expression shape reports only the unbroken run of agreeing arms directly above a total `_` arm, as one finding carrying one deletion per arm. Reporting each separately gives skala fix several edits for one finding; reporting only the lowest leaves a finding standing on the fix's own output. An arm with a when clause is not inert even when its value agrees, and a pattern that binds a name makes two syntactically identical expressions mean different things — both withdraw. ⚠ The whole-switch collapse ReSharper also offers is deliberately not done: replacing the switch with the value stops evaluating the governing expression.
